claims.text: The Bateau-Lavoir is an incredibly famous building in art history, known as the early residence and meeting place for some of the world's greatest artists.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Originally operating as a ballroom and piano factory, it was converted into 20 small, unheated artist workshops in 1889.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Pablo Picasso himself lived here, painting some of his most famous masterpieces, including 'Les Demoiselles d'Avignon' in 1907.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The name translates to 'Washhouse Boat', a nickname coined by French poet Max Jacob because the dark, creaky building reminded him of washing-boats floating on the Seine.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: Sadly, a massive fire destroyed almost the entire original building in 1970, miraculously leaving only its original facade standing.
claims.subject: self

claims.text: The structure was successfully rebuilt in 1978, and today it actually still functions as a creative home, continuing to house working artist studios.
claims.subject: self
